## What's new

Threadnote 5.3.4 makes memory writes and recall more responsive, adds reliable index preparation, and improves workflow and process visibility.

### Prepare lexical and semantic recall together

`threadnote index rebuild` waits for both lexical search and semantic recall to be ready for the inputs it inspected. Source, model, or authorization drift is reported instead of presenting an outdated rebuild as current. Routine vector maintenance stays asynchronous; use this command when you need foreground confirmation that both indexes are ready.

### Track longer memory writes

Longer MCP memory saves can return a trackable pending operation instead of holding the client open. Success still requires the canonical write and required lexical checks to finish. Optional context preparation and derived maintenance run outside protected foreground writes where possible; explicit synchronization and repair commands retain their requested completion behavior.

### Read ready context without foreground repairs

Ordinary recall, canonical reads, and Context Brief use compatible ready snapshots instead of starting a full rebuild in the read path. Missing, stale, budget-exhausted, and failed reads remain distinguishable, with useful partial results and explicit warnings where available.

Final selected results are checked against current canonical content and access after optional inference, rather than reusing cached authority. Exact-match anchors and normal sibling relevance are preserved. Query cancellation verifies owned-worker shutdown and reports when cleanup cannot be confirmed.

### See which processes are doing the work

Manager shows CPU and memory use with workspace, client, and foreground/background lane context, including owned workers. Recall-read workers have a clear process role, making active work and resource use easier to follow.

### Keep Manager connections current

Connection lists show pending state and retry guidance while preparation completes, keeping the canonical document available. Stale neighbor links and editor navigation are cleared after writes or navigation changes, and late results from an older view cannot replace newer content.

### Keep development reviews tied to current source

Development workflows distinguish implementation from independent correctness, simplicity, and specialist reviews. Base and stacked-proof checks keep evidence tied to current source while preserving phase and review history. Larger phased plans retain their full approved file scope through export and validation.

### Keep graph discovery and cleanup bounded

Code-graph updates use compact, file-owned candidate evidence with bounded discovery and cleanup. Protected snapshots remain retained, and incomplete evidence uses safe fallback discovery instead of being treated as proof that nothing was found.
